standard_prerequisites: Dependent pair types with their projections.
The characterization of paths in dependent pair types as pairs of a base path and a path over it (the retained context).
Transport along a path with its definitional behaviour on reflexivity, and reflexivity paths.
core_obligations: Prove, for every element z of a dependent pair type, the identification of z with the pair of its projections.
Reduce the identification to the over-path component using the path characterization of dependent pair types, and settle it by the definitional computation of transport on reflexivity.
proof_roadmap: By the path characterization for Sigma types (the retained context), an identification of z with the pair of its projections amounts to a base path between the first projections together with an identification of the transported second component with the second projection of the pair.

Base component: reflexivity of the first projection identifies the first projection of z with the first projection of the pair of projections, since the first projection of the pair of projections is definitionally the first projection of z.

Over component: the required identification is between the transport of the second projection of z along reflexivity and the second projection of the pair of projections; both sides are definitionally the second projection of z, so reflexivity suffices.
Conclude the identification of z with its pair of projections.
difficulty_reason: A short application of the Sigma-type path characterization; the base and over components both settle by definitional computation on reflexivity.
